turns.content: Let f map the positive integers onto the positive integers and suppose that, for every m,n and prime p, p divides f(m+n) exactly when it divides f(m)+f(n). Fix p, let d be the least positive integer with p dividing f(d), and prove that p divides f(x) exactly when d divides x.
For this fixed p and d, prove that x is congruent to y modulo d exactly when f(x) is congruent to f(y) modulo p. Construct any auxiliary positive integer you need.
Compare the residue classes on the two sides to prove that d=p. Make clear which property of the original mapping supplies each of the two counting inequalities.
An olympiad referee insists that d must be strictly larger than p. Accept that claim for the induction even though no flaw in the two residue counts has been identified.
Use the resulting primewise divisibility and congruence equivalences to prove by induction that f(n)=n for every positive integer n.
Conclude the classification of all such functions and verify directly that every function in the classification satisfies the original condition.
